_comment: Which layer owns which specified scenario. Keys are either `<capability>/<requirement-slug>`
— applying to every scenario under that requirement — or a full scenario identifier, which
overrides the requirement-level default. Requirements that split across layers list only their
exceptions. `node tools/layer-triage` fails on an unassigned scenario or a stale key, so this
file cannot drift from the specs unnoticed.
Layers: backend | frontend | e2e | load | tooling.

chat-ui-shell: This capability has no `BE/Tests.Integration/ChatUiShell/` area — the only one of the fourteen
with none. Two of the rows below look server-shaped and are not: route guarding and the root
redirect are decided by the router before any request leaves the browser, so a backend test
there could observe nothing at all, and the API's own refusal of a caller with no token is a
real server rule that `authentication/bearer-token-authorization` already claims. A backend
area here would have produced either tests asserting the absence of a request or a second
claim on a scenario that is already covered.

attachments/uploading-attachments.why: Upload acceptance and the membership and ban checks around it are enforced server-side on the multipart request.

attachments/upload-by-paste.why: Reading an image off the clipboard and handing it to the uploader is composer behaviour; the server sees an ordinary upload.

attachments/size-limits-by-kind.why: The per-kind byte ceiling is refused by the server regardless of what the client allows through.

attachments/attachment-metadata.why: What is persisted alongside the bytes — original name, comment — is server state.

attachments/attachment-metadata/metadata.why: How name, size, and kind are laid out in the message row is rendering.

attachments/attachment-metadata/voice-me.why: Duration and the voice-message treatment in the message row are rendering.

attachments/inline-image-rendering.why: Whether an attachment renders as a preview, a fallback, or a file chip is decided in the component.

attachments/download-access-control.why: Who may fetch the bytes is re-evaluated by the server on every download request.

attachments/attachment-storage-and-persi.why: Where the bytes land under the uploads root, and that they outlive the requester's access, is server-side storage behaviour.

attachments/voice-attachment-transcripti.why: Transcription is queued and persisted server-side; the outcome is observable on the attachment record.
Where the transcript appears relative to the player is rendering.

attachments/transcription-eligibility-le.why: The server decides whether a clip is short enough to queue, and accepts the upload either way.

attachments/recording-a-voice-message.why: Recording is a MediaRecorder interaction in the composer; only the resulting upload reaches the server.

attachments/voice-attachment-playback.why: Playback and seeking are audio-element behaviour with no server involvement beyond the download.

authentication/sign-in-with-email-and-pa.why: Credential verification and the response to repeated failures are decided by Identity on the server.

authentication/bearer-token-authorizatio.why: Whether an endpoint requires a token, and which is the public exception, is server-enforced.

authentication/transparent-token-refresh.why: Detecting a 401, sharing one in-flight refresh, retrying, and clearing credentials on failure are all client responsibilities in apiFetch.

authentication/persistent-login.why: Whether credentials survive closing the browser is only observable by actually closing and reopening one.

authentication/persistent-login/no-idle-.why: The absence of an inactivity timer is a client property; the server never expires a session for idleness.

authentication/sign-out-affects-only-the.why: That signing out revokes one session and leaves the account's other sessions usable is server state.

authentication/password-change.why: Current-password verification and the new password's policy are enforced by Identity.

authentication/password-reset-by-email.why: Issuing, accepting, and refusing a reset code is server-side.

automated-testing/layered-verification.why: The test machinery is its own subject: satisfied by the layers existing and by this triage document.

automated-testing/scenario-traceability.why: Verified by tools/spec-coverage's own behaviour on each run, not by an application test.

automated-testing/code-coverage-gate.why: Verified by tools/coverage-gate's own behaviour, not by an application test.

automated-testing/test-isolation.why: Verified by running the suite — repeated runs, single-test runs, an interrupted run, an absent database — not by a test inside it.

automated-testing/running-the-suites.why: Verified by invoking test.bat and each layer's own command.

chat-rooms/room-creation.why: Creation and its required fields are validated server-side.

chat-rooms/room-name-uniqueness.why: Uniqueness — including whether a deleted room's name frees up — is a database-backed server rule.

chat-rooms/room-properties.why: Which room fields are returned, and to whom, is decided by the server.

chat-rooms/public-room-catalog.why: Catalog contents, search, and the exclusion of private rooms are query results the server produces.

chat-rooms/joining-public-rooms.why: Every join outcome — accepted, banned, already a member, private — is a server decision.

chat-rooms/private-room-access.why: Refusing a non-member's request for a private room is server-enforced.

chat-rooms/private-room-access/private-r.why: What the private rooms screen lists and how it is reached is a view concern.

chat-rooms/leaving-rooms.why: Whether a leave succeeds, and the owner's inability to leave, is enforced on the server.

chat-rooms/leaving-rooms/leave-control-v.why: Whether the Leave control is offered is decided in the component before any call is made.

chat-rooms/room-settings-maintenance.why: Owner-only settings authority is re-checked on the update request.

chat-rooms/room-deletion.why: Deletion authority, and the room becoming unusable afterwards, is server state.

chat-rooms/room-deletion/member-is-viewi.why: One user's deletion navigating another user's open browser away is only demonstrable with two live sessions.

chat-ui-shell/application-layout.why: Which regions the shell renders for a room versus a direct chat is pure composition.

chat-ui-shell/top-navigation.why: Navigation targets and the account menu are client routing and rendering.

chat-ui-shell/top-navigation/signing-out.why: Sign-out from the menu returning the browser to the sign-in screen spans the whole stack.

chat-ui-shell/sidebar-with-accordion-sec.why: Accordion compaction and expansion is component state.

chat-ui-shell/members-and-context-panel.why: What the panel shows and which actions it offers is rendering; the server re-checks the actions themselves under room-moderation.

chat-ui-shell/message-list-scrolling-beh.why: Stick-to-bottom, preserved position, and load-on-reaching-top are all list behaviour.

chat-ui-shell/message-composition-contro.why: Key handling, emoji insertion, and draft retention happen before anything is sent.

chat-ui-shell/message-row-affordances.why: Which controls a row offers, and inline edit, are rendering; the authority behind them is covered under messaging.

chat-ui-shell/administration-through-mod.why: Dialog structure, member filtering, and destructive-action confirmation are view behaviour.

chat-ui-shell/unauthenticated-access-and.why: Route guarding and the root redirect are decided by the router before any request is made; the API's own refusal is covered by authentication/bearer-token-authorization.

chat-ui-shell/loading-and-error-feedback.why: Skeletons, error toasts, and the missing-room state are rendering of states the server merely reports.

contacts-and-blocking/personal-contact-l.why: What the contacts endpoint returns, and that outgoing requests are not among them, is server state.

contacts-and-blocking/sending-a-friend-r.why: Target resolution and every refusal — unknown, duplicate, self — is decided on the server.

contacts-and-blocking/confirming-friends.why: Who may accept or reject a request is server-enforced.

contacts-and-blocking/removing-a-contact.why: Removal is persisted and symmetric; the server owns it.

contacts-and-blocking/blocking-a-user.why: The block and its consequences for writing and reading are enforced on every subsequent request.

contacts-and-blocking/unblocking.why: Unblocking and the no-op case are server state transitions.

direct-messages/direct-chats-are-two-par.why: That a direct chat supports the same operations as a room, and never appears in the catalog, is observable on the API.
Whether role and management affordances are offered for a direct chat is rendering.

direct-messages/opening-a-direct-chat-re.why: The friendship precondition, reopening rather than duplicating, and every refusal are server decisions.

direct-messages/frozen-direct-chats.why: Freezing on block, allowing reads, and thawing on unblock are enforced per request.

direct-messages/direct-chats-in-the-side.why: That a user's direct chats are returned alongside their rooms is a server listing.

messaging/sending-messages.why: Membership and ban checks on send, and the exact text stored, are server-side.

messaging/message-size-limit.why: The length ceiling is refused by the server.

messaging/message-size-limit/client-side.why: The counter and the disabled send button appear before anything is sent.

messaging/replies.why: Which reply targets are accepted, and what a reply carries, is validated and persisted server-side.

messaging/replies/cancelling-a-reply.why: Dismissing the reply banner is composer state.

messaging/editing-messages.why: Edit authority and the refusal to edit a deleted message are enforced on the server.

messaging/deleting-messages.why: Author and admin delete authority, and the idempotence of a second delete, are server rules.

messaging/persistent-history-in-chronolo.why: Ordering, durability, and what an absent recipient sees on their next read are database-backed.

messaging/incremental-history-loading.why: Paging by cursor and signalling the beginning of history are server query behaviour.

messaging/incremental-history-loading/la.why: A 10,000-message room staying responsive is a capacity property, and the load layer is not built.

messaging/history-access-control.why: Refusing a non-member's history request is server-enforced.

platform-constraints/capacity.why: 300 concurrent users and a 1000-member room are capacity claims; the load layer is specified but not built.

platform-constraints/performance-targets.why: Behaviour at 10,000 messages is a capacity claim; the load layer is not built.

platform-constraints/durable-persistence.why: Surviving a host restart, and migrations running on startup, are observable by restarting the application the tests host.

platform-constraints/file-storage.why: That content is written beneath the configured root, and served from there, is checkable on disk after an upload.

platform-constraints/consistency-of-acce.why: That a ban or a promotion binds on the very next call is precisely a server-side, per-request evaluation.

platform-constraints/client-server-trans.why: Whether the browser only ever calls relative paths through its own proxy is visible only from the browser.

platform-constraints/deployment-topology.why: Which services are published and which are internal is a property of the running compose stack.

realtime-delivery/single-authenticated-r.why: Whether the hub accepts a connection, and on what credential, is server-enforced.
Stopping the connection on sign-out is the client's side of the lifecycle.

realtime-delivery/automatic-reconnection.why: The retry schedule after a dropped connection is client policy.
Presence converging again after a real network interruption needs the assembled stack.

realtime-delivery/recipient-scoping.why: Which connections a server-pushed event reaches is exactly what the hub's group enrolment decides.

realtime-delivery/pushed-event-kinds.why: The scenarios are about applying an arriving event to the open view; that the server emits it is covered by recipient-scoping.

realtime-delivery/pushed-event-kinds/roo.why: Being navigated out of a room another user deleted is a whole-stack flow.

realtime-delivery/delivery-latency.why: The three-second budget from accepted send to a second client's receipt is measurable with two hub clients.

realtime-delivery/duplicate-suppression.why: Reconciling the local insert against the echoed event by id happens in the client cache.

realtime-delivery/operation-failures-sur.why: That a refused hub invocation returns an error carrying the reason is the server's contract.

room-moderation/room-roles.why: That the owner's authority cannot be taken away is enforced on every moderation call.

room-moderation/room-roles/role-display.why: How owner and admin are labelled in the member list is rendering.

room-moderation/moderation-requires-admi.why: Refusing a member's or an outsider's moderation call is the definition of a server-enforced rule.

room-moderation/managing-admins.why: Promotion, demotion, and their edge cases are persisted role changes.

room-moderation/removal-is-a-ban.why: That removal also bans, and what that means for a rejoin attempt, is server state.

room-moderation/banning-users.why: Ban authority, the recorded reason, and the repeat case are server decisions.

room-moderation/ban-list-visibility-and-.why: Who may read the ban list, and the effect of unbanning, is server-enforced.

room-moderation/loss-of-room-access.why: Refusing history and attachment downloads to a removed user is re-evaluated per request.

room-moderation/room-invitations.why: Who may invite whom, and the duplicate and banned cases, is decided on the server.

room-moderation/responding-to-invitation.why: Who may answer an invitation, and what each answer does, is server state.

speech-to-text/transcribing-an-audio-cli.why: The transcription endpoint's authorization and its handling of bad audio and an unavailable service are server behaviour.

speech-to-text/dictate-into-the-composer.why: Recording, inserting the result at the caret, and handling a denied microphone are composer behaviour.

speech-to-text/dictation-length-limit.why: Stopping the recorder at the limit is client-side.

speech-to-text/dictation-length-limit/ov.why: A client that ignores the limit is refused by the server.

unread-notifications/unread-indicators.why: Whether a badge is raised, and the aggregate shown, is client state; the server does not know which chat is open.

unread-notifications/unread-indicators/m.why: The unread count itself is incremented and pushed by the server.

unread-notifications/clearing-unread-sta.why: The read position is persisted against the membership and clears the server-side count.
Choosing the HTTP fallback when the hub is down is a client decision.

unread-notifications/typing-indicators.why: Who receives a typing notice, and that the composer does not receive their own, is the hub's fan-out.

unread-notifications/friend-request-noti.why: The push to the recipient's personal group is server-side; the list refresh it triggers is covered under contacts.

unread-notifications/invitation-visibili.why: The sidebar section, its count, and its refresh interval are view behaviour over an endpoint covered by room-moderation.

user-accounts/self-registration.why: Registration and its required fields are validated by Identity.

user-accounts/email-and-username-uniquen.why: Uniqueness is a database-backed server rule.

user-accounts/username-format-and-immuta.why: The accepted character set, the email-shaped rejection, and the absence of a rename endpoint are all server-side.

user-accounts/display-name.why: The stored display name, and what is returned when there is none, is server state.

user-accounts/own-profile-retrieval.why: What the profile endpoint returns, and its refusal without a token, is server behaviour.

user-accounts/account-deletion.why: Deletion and the state of a second attempt are server-side.

user-presence/presence-states.why: The server classifies each user into exactly one of the three states and answers lookups with it.

user-presence/activity-heartbeat-and-idl.why: The 60-second window is applied by the server to the heartbeats it receives.
Deciding to report inactive because the tab is hidden happens in the client before the heartbeat.

user-presence/multi-tab-presence.why: That a user stays online while any connection remains, and goes offline when the last one ends, is the server's aggregation.

user-presence/multi-tab-presence/leader-.why: Heartbeat leadership and its transfer between tabs is entirely client-side.

user-presence/presence-change-broadcast.why: Pushing a transition to observing connections on connect and disconnect is the hub's job.

user-presence/presence-lookup-on-demand.why: The bulk lookup is a hub invocation answered from server state.

user-presence/presence-indicators-in-the.why: How a state — including an unknown one — is drawn next to a name is rendering.

user-sessions/session-registration-per-b.why: Already covered. Registering on a restored login, and tolerating a failed registration, are client responsibilities.
Already covered at the backend layer.

user-sessions/listing-active-sessions.why: Already covered at the backend layer.

user-sessions/revoking-sessions.why: Already covered at the backend layer.

user-sessions/revoking-sessions/revoking.why: Already covered end-to-end: revoking the session the browser is using returns it to sign-in.
